claims.text: An interface-pinning free-energy sampling method implemented within an ab initio DFT framework can accurately predict melting temperature.
The method can accurately predict entropy of fusion.
The method can accurately predict enthalpy of fusion.
The method can accurately predict volume change at melting.
The proposed method has significantly lower computational cost than full thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamics.
A two-phase free-energy sampling algorithm can replace full thermodynamic integration and be implemented directly within a DFT framework.
The method requires or benefits from clear solid-liquid coexistence near the melting point.
The energetics of the solid-liquid interface mediate the phase transition and underpin the proposed free-energy sampling method.
Stabilizing the solid-liquid interface and sampling its fluctuations determines the free-energy difference between solid and liquid phases.
Interface stabilization and fluctuation sampling avoid extensive integration over thermodynamic paths.
The resulting solid-liquid free-energy differences yield melting temperature, fusion entropy, fusion enthalpy, and volume change at melting.
Avoiding extensive thermodynamic-path integration lowers computational expense.
The proposed approach will agree within acceptable error margins with conventional thermodynamic-integration results.
The proposed approach will use substantially fewer computational resources than conventional thermodynamic integration.
Reduced computational cost will enable high-throughput evaluations of melting properties.
Conventional ab initio molecular dynamics with full thermodynamic integration is precise.
Conventional ab initio molecular dynamics with full thermodynamic integration is computationally expensive.
The approach is expected to be applicable to materials with well-defined solid-liquid interfaces.
A complex free-energy landscape may limit the applicability of the approach.
Failure of interface pinning to capture significant fluctuations in some materials may limit the approach.
